html_reuse.scope: Reuse only the passing HTML result; the same source original fast gate failed and is retained. Final relocated source has its own passing full selected tests and fast gate.

acceptance: The bounded schema catalogs sixteen settings, three optional atom columns and two original detached assignment reports.
Native dtype/null semantics, lists/tuples, exact large integer arrays, field/unit/dimension integrity and source/projection provenance are guarded.
All 67 new codec cases and existing 0.3/0.4/0.5 persistence, native dictionaries, trusted checkpoints and composition guards pass: 1,178 tests with no omissions.
Three actual complete/projected/nonpolar-H-merged preparations load in new processes with different output units, no RDKit/OpenMM/Ackredit or recalculation, and original producer metadata retained.
Bulk arrays remain HDF5 datasets; fixed-width UTF-8 block transfers avoid variable-length string heaps. The 100,000-element representation guard is not a performance benchmark.
Initial dtype/NA-buffer and UTF-8 memory-type failures and the failed adapter-only layout gate remain recorded. Final placement is private storage; the validator is unchanged.
limits: Public writing/reading remains H5MSM 0.5. No root 0.6/1.0 implementation or default-writer switch is introduced.
P3/P4 still need whole-file associations, publication semantics and public operations. P5/P6 retain full prepared-system/client/platform and final format qualification.
No massive-system memory/disk performance, arbitrary object/dtype, multi-parameterization or engine-state claim is made.
Only the unchanged HTML scope is reused from d3e6b1ac7; its original 13/14 fast result remains failed. Final source passes its own 14/14 fast result.
#256/#438 remain open. No weighted milestone, graphical intent or source-issue closure is added.

corrections.explanation: The H5MSM module-location review is #438. #441 is an unrelated closed distance bug; its misplaced comment was corrected. Executed runs, code, data hashes and outcomes are unchanged.
